column1: # The REST surface of the dispatch service.
# THIS FILE IS THE EXPECTATION. It is written by hand from TAR-0004 section 3
# (the twenty-five calls, on MCP and REST under the same names) and from the
# concept document's section 3 (what each call takes), in the path form of the
# adapter this surface replaced. It is deliberately NOT derived from the built
# code: a probe that reads its expectation out of the thing it probes checks
# that two copies agree, never that either is right.
#   verb      the call's name on REST (the assistant surface prefixes
#             `dispatch_`), or '-' where the row names no call
#   path      the form, exactly as it must appear
#   repeat    what makes a repeat safe: idempotency-key, conflict-token,
# THE CALLS -- one route each, and no route without one
# Sixteen transitions and nine calls that are not transitions. A call that is
# not the plain read, write or delete of what its path names is a custom
# method in colon notation; the colon is forced, because the id part may grow
# segments and a trailing verb segment could not be told from one.
# What the framework may have registered. Probed STATICALLY against the
# annotations, and that is the closure half: a route outside this list is a
# violation, whatever it does. There are fewer bindings than calls, and the
# reason is measured rather than chosen: a path template takes the whole
# segment it appears in (Quarkus REST 3.33.2, 2026-09-01), so the colon is
# split off in the adapter from a table the probe reads separately.
# REST is extensible while an extension adds no effect: reads, projections,
# protocol furniture. State changes come from a call, without exception.
